## The claim

The detection limit of the fold-over B-deviation test is at most 10 percent cell fraction for every autosome at this sample's heterozygous-site count and depth.

**Prediction if true.** The simulated smallest detectable fraction at 80 percent power is no greater than 0.10 for each of the 22 autosomes.

**What would refute it.** Any autosome whose limit exceeds 0.10 -- that chromosome is named as a blind spot and no absence claim is made for it.

## Evidence

Nothing observed yet. This claim is proposed, not tested.
